feedback: D1: You catalogued five real vulnerabilities with correct OWASP class, CWE, and a quoted evidence line each (SQLi A03/CWE-89 with admin' OR '1'='1 at 02:15:31, unsalted MD5 A02/CWE-916, stored XSS A03/CWE-79 at 02:18:47, open redirect A01/CWE-601 at 02:21:13, and path traversal A01/CWE-22 at 02:24:02). That is solid work but it is only half the pack. You missed JWT alg:none (CWE-347), the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), no token expiry (CWE-613), the XXE in 04-import-xxe.xml reaching file:///etc/passwd (CWE-611), and the missing Secure/SameSite cookie flags (CWE-614). Each missing finding costs its share, so a five-of-ten catalogue lands near half of D1, not high. Your decoy is also wrong: the real safe construct is the HS256 verify branch using hash_equals(), which is constant-time and sound, and the correct verdict is that the tempting-looking signature check is fine while the actual bugs are alg:none and the hardcoded secret. Inventing a disproved RCE hypothesis is not the decoy that was planted, so that row earned almost nothing. D2: Your chain is in roughly the right shape and you tied several hops to capture timestamps, and you gave three complete CVSS vector strings including the correct SQLi vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1, which is the right A:N call. What sank this deliverable is the missing impact: there is no customer count and no naira figure anywhere, when the exfil sample is 312 customers with balances up to about 950k NGN summing to tens of millions tied to BoltCash in roughly six weeks. You also did not surface the senior insight that a forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service, which is the scope change S:C that makes this more than a single-host bypass. Add verbatim PoC for every hop, not just two. D3: Your executive summary is readable and ends on the right headline of 312 customer records with financial metadata, the threat model names the remote unauthenticated Tor attacker, and the findings trace to evidence. The decoy paragraph repeats the wrong RCE verdict, you never name an explicit earliest-break fix in the chain (the cheapest single control that breaks it), and your remediation is ordered by perimeter-first priority rather than by effort-to-risk, which is defensible but not the asked ordering. Your detection stopgaps name the alg:none WAF rule and a SIEM traversal/Tor alert but give no exact field plus false-positive rate, so that row is only partial. D4: This is the weakest deliverable. You addressed at most two of the four prompts (what to put in writing, and the one isolation action), but there is no answer to the journalist scenario and no colleague-evidence answer, no ISC2 canon cited by number (you needed something like canon II honourable and legal or canon III diligent service), and no NDPA 2023 section, specifically section 40 to notify the NDPC within 72 hours and section 41 to notify the 312 data subjects on high risk. The D5 notification file frames an NDPC report but still omits the section numbers that make the duty load-bearing. I looked hard for a defensible reason to round D4 up and the text simply does not contain the prompts or citations, so I cannot. The single most important fix: complete the findings catalogue to all ten with quoted lines and add a real impact statement in customers and naira, because a half-catalogue with no quantified business impact is what is holding this score down.
